name: Korvain Dynamics Explosive Ordnance Disposal Suit
description:
A blast-rated suit weighing approximately 27 kilograms, designed to protect the wearer from fragmentation, overpressure, and thermal effects of explosive detonation at close range. The suit uses layered ballistic fabric over rigid plate inserts, with a reinforced helmet and face shield rated for direct fragmentation impact.

EOD operators refer to putting on this suit as 'suiting up for a conversation' — the conversation being between them and a device that might or might not respond to their disarming attempt. The suit can save their life if the conversation goes badly. It cannot guarantee it.
functionality: Blast fragmentation protection, overpressure mitigation, thermal barrier
what_it_says: You walk toward things that are designed to kill everyone nearby, and you do it slowly and deliberately.
story_hooks: An EOD suit is found with blast damage consistent with an explosion — but the operator wearing it is missing, and the detonation site shows no biological evidence that anyone was inside when it went off.

physical_description.visual_profile: A bulky, utilitarian silhouette dominated by rigid segmented plating and thick fabric layering. The suit presents as an armored second skin with deliberate industrial geometry—high shoulders, articulated joints, reinforced torso. Despite its mass, it reads as purposefully engineered rather than crude, with clean lines between plate sections and fabric zones.
physical_description.fit: Heavily oversized and deliberately loose-fitted to accommodate rapid donning/doffing and allow air circulation. The suit sits away from the body with intentional gaps at joints for articulation. Movement is restricted but calculated—every looseness serves blast dispersion.
physical_description.primary_material: Layered ballistic weave composite (kevlar-grade synth-aramid blend) over rigid high-density polymer plates and steel inserts at critical zones. The face shield is reinforced polycarbonate-titanium hybrid rated for fragmentation.
physical_description.texture: Heavy and heavily textured—quilted ballistic sections, rough industrial plating with utilitarian matte finish, ribbed reinforcement panels along stress points. Multiple material transitions create visual texture breaks. The helmet has a slightly weathered, scuffed appearance.
physical_description.color_scheme: Industrial grey-black base with high-visibility reflective trim at shoulders, wrists, and torso front. Accent striping in safety orange/yellow along plate seams. Worn stainless steel hardware and dull gunmetal plating. The face shield tints slightly amber when viewed head-on.
physical_description.closures: Heavy-duty magnetic release latches at shoulders for rapid suit removal, reinforced friction-fit seals at neck and wrists, multi-point velcro anchors at waist and thighs, locking collar mechanism.
distinctive_features: Integrated cooling channels visible as subtle ribbed patterns beneath outer fabric
Manufacturer's Korvain Dynamics logo embossed on left chest plate
Oversized reinforced gloves with segmented finger articulation and grip-rated palms
Heavy-duty visor with interior anti-glare coating and slight optical distortion
Mounting points for sensor arrays and communication equipment on helmet crown
Explosive-rated cabling visible at joint areas—deliberate exposure of internal structure
Inspection markings and blast-test certification stamps on torso
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 1-2 specialized equipment (expensive, corporation-issued, high-tech), though the wearer is typically working-class Tier 3-4 hazmat operator
physical_description.cultural_context: Military/paramilitary/specialized hazmat operator. Signals someone who regularly converses with devices that explode. Worn by EOD teams, bomb disposal units, hazmat contractors. The suit itself is a job description and a prayer.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained but bearing visible scars—small blast scoring on plating, minor cracks in non-critical areas repaired with matching material, dust and grime buildup in crevices. The suit is worn regularly and respected. It shows professional use, not negligence.
